source: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Series Command Reference (A-H, I-R, S, T-Z)

commands.name: aaa accounting command
commands.description: To send accounting messages to the TACACS+ accounting server when you enter any command other than show commands at the CLI, use the aaa accounting command command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa accounting console
commands.syntax: aaa accounting {serial | telnet | ssh | enable} console server-tag
commands.description: To enable support for AAA accounting for administrative access, use the aaa accounting console command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa accounting include, exclude
commands.syntax: aaa accounting {include | exclude} service interface_name inside_ip inside_mask [outside_ip outside_mask] server_tag
commands.description: To enable accounting for TCP or UDP connections through the ASA, use the aaa accounting include command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa accounting match
commands.syntax: aaa accounting match acl_name interface_name server_tag
commands.description: To enable accounting for TCP and UDP connections through the ASA, use the aaa accounting match command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authentication console
commands.syntax: aaa authentication {serial | enable | telnet | ssh | http} console {LOCAL | server_group [LOCAL]}
commands.description: To authenticate users who access the ASA CLI over a serial, SSH, HTTPS (ASDM), or Telnet connection, or to authenticate users who access privileged EXEC mode using the enable command, use the aaa authentication console command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authentication include, exclude
commands.syntax: aaa authentication {include | exclude} service interface_name inside_ip inside_mask [outside_ip outside_mask] {server_tag | LOCAL}
commands.description: To enable authentication for connections through the ASA, use the aaa authentication include command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authentication listener
commands.syntax: aaa authentication listener {http | https} interface_name [port portnum] [redirect]
commands.description: To enable HTTP/HTTPS listening ports to authenticate network users, use the aaa authentication listener command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authentication listener no-logout-button
commands.description: To remove the logout button from the cut-through proxy portal page, use the aaa authentication listener no-logout-button command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authentication login-history
commands.description: To set the login history duration, use the aaa authentication login-history command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authentication match
commands.syntax: aaa authentication match acl_name interface_name {server_tag | LOCAL} user-identity
commands.description: To enable authentication for connections through the ASA, use the aaa authentication match command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authentication secure-http-client
commands.description: To enable SSL and secure username and password exchange between HTTP clients and the ASA, use the aaa authentication secure-http-client command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authorization command
commands.description: To enable command authorization, use the aaa authorization command command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authorization exec
commands.description: To enable management authorization, use the aaa authorization exec command o in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authorization exec ssh-x509
commands.description: To enable SSH authorization for X.509v3-certificate-authenticated users, use the aaa authorization exec ssh-x509 command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authorization http
commands.syntax: Syntax Description aaa-server-group Defined already, and the protocol configured for the aaa-server-group must be LDAP, RADIUS, or TACACS+. The command will have no effect if the protocol is not LDAP, RADIUS, or TACACS+. console Specify this keyword to identify a server group for administrative authorization. LOCAL Predefined server tag for AAA protocol ‘local’
commands.description: To enable authorization for ASDM, use the aaa authorization http command.

commands.name: aaa authorization include, exclude
commands.syntax: aaa authorization {include | exclude} service interface_name inside_ip inside_mask [outside_ip outside_mask server_tag
commands.description: To enable authorization for connections through the ASA, use the aaa authorization include command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa authorization match
commands.syntax: aaa authorization match acl_name interface_name server_tag
commands.description: To enable authorization for connections through the ASA, use the aaa authorization match command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa kerberos import-keytab
commands.description: To import a Kerberos keytab file so that it can be used to authenticate the Kerberos server, use the aaa kerberos import-keytab command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa local authentication attempts max-fail
commands.syntax: aaa local authentication attempts max-fail number
commands.description: To limit the number of consecutive failed local login attempts that the ASA allows any given user account, use the aaa local authentication attempts max-fail command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa mac-exempt
commands.description: To specify the use of a predefined list of MAC addresses to exempt from authentication and authorization, use the aaa mac-exempt command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa proxy-limit
commands.description: To limit the number of concurrent authentication attempts (at the same time) for a given IP address, use the aaa proxy-limit command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa sdi import-node-secret
commands.syntax: aaa sdi import-node-secret filepath rsa_server_address password
commands.description: To import a node secret file that you exported from an RSA Authentication Manager for use with an SDI AAA server group, use the aaa sdi import-node-secret command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa-server
commands.description: To create a AAA server group and configure AAA server parameters that are group-specific and common to all group hosts, use the aaa-server command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: aaa-server active, fail
commands.description: To reactivate a AAA server that is marked failed, use the aaa-server active command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: aaa-server host
commands.description: To configure a AAA server as part of a AAA server group and to configure AAA server parameters that are host-specific, use the aaa-server host command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: absolute
commands.description: To define an absolute time when a time range is in effect, use the absolute command in time-range configuration mode.

commands.name: accept-subordinates
commands.description: To configure the ASA to accept subordinate CA certificates if delivered during phase one IKE exchange when not previously installed on the device, use the accept-subordinates command in crypto ca trustpoint configuration mode.

commands.name: access-group
commands.syntax: access-group access_list {in | out} interface interface_name [per-user-override / control-plane]
commands.description: To bind an extended or Ethertype ACL to a single interface, use the access-group command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: access-list alert-interval
commands.description: To specify the time interval between deny flow maximum messages, use the access-list alert-interval command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: access-list deny-flow-max
commands.description: To specify the maximum number of concurrent deny flows that can be cached for calculating statistics for message 106100, use the access-list deny-flow-max command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: access-list ethertype
commands.syntax: access-list id ethertype {deny | permit} {any | bpdu | dsap {hex_address | bpdu | ipx | isis | raw-ipx} | eii-ipx | ipx | isis | mpls-unicast | mpls-multicast | hex_number}
commands.description: To configure an ACL that controls traffic based on its EtherType, use the access-list ethertype command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: access-list extended
commands.syntax: access-list access_list_name [line line_number] extended {deny | permit} protocol_argument [user_argument] [security_group_argument] source_address_argument [security_group_argument] dest_address_argument [log [[level] interval secs] | disable | default]] [time-range time_range_name] [inactive]
commands.description: To add an Access Control Entry (ACE) to an extended ACL, use the access-list extended command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: access-list remark
commands.description: To specify the text of a remark to add before or after an extended, EtherType, or standard access control entry, use the access-list remark command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: access-list rename
commands.description: To rename an ACL, use the access-list rename command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: access-list standard
commands.syntax: access-list id standard {deny | permit} {any4 | host ip_address | ip_address subnet_mask}
commands.description: To add an Access Control Entry (ACE) to a standard ACL, use the access-list standard command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: access-list webtype
commands.syntax: access-list id webtype {deny | permit} url {url_string | any} [log [[level] [interval secs] | disable | default]]} [time_range name] [inactive]
commands.description: To add an Access Control Entry (ACE) to a webtype ACL, which filters clientless SSL VPN connections, use the access-list webtype command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: accounting-mode
commands.description: To indicate whether accounting messages are sent to a single server (single mode) or sent to all servers in the group (simultaneous mode), use the accounting-mode command in aaa-server configuration mode.

commands.name: accounting-port
commands.description: To specify the port number used for RADIUS accounting for this host, use the accounting-port command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: accounting-server-group
commands.description: To specify the AAA server group for sending accounting records, use the accounting-server-group command in various modes.
commands.mode: Imap4s configuration (deprecated), pop3s configuration (deprecated), Smtps configuration (deprecated), Tunnel-group general-attributes configuration

commands.name: acl-netmask-convert
commands.description: To specify how the ASA treats netmasks received in a downloadable ACL from a RADIUS server that is accessed by using the aaa-server host command, use the acl-netmask-convert command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: action
commands.description: To either apply access policies to a session or terminate the session, use the action command in dynamic-access-policy-record configuration mode.

commands.name: action cli command
commands.description: To configure actions on an event manager applet, use the action cli command command in event manager applet configuration mode.

commands.name: action-uri
commands.description: To specify a web server URI to receive a username and password for single sign-on (SSO) authentication, use the action-uri command in aaa-server-host configuration mode.

commands.name: activate-tunnel-group-script
commands.description: This command is used internally to reload an ASDM generated script file when username-from-certificate is configured in tunnel-group sub-mode.

commands.name: activation-key
commands.description: To enter a license activation key on the ASA, use the activation-key command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: activex-relay
commands.description: To incorporate applications that need ActiveX over the clientless portal, use the activex-relay command in group-policy webvpn configuration mode or username webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group-policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: ad-agent-mode
commands.description: To enables the AD Agent mode so that you can configure the Active Directory Agent for the Cisco Identify Firewall instance, use the ad-agent-mode command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: address (dynamic-filter blacklist, whitelist)
commands.description: To add an IP address to the Botnet Traffic Filter blacklist or whitelist, use the address command in dynamic-filter blacklist or whitelist configuration mode.

commands.name: address (media-termination)
commands.description: To specify the address for a media termination instance to use for media connections to the Phone Proxy feature, use the address command in the media-termination configuration mode.

commands.name: address-family ipv4
commands.description: To enter address family to configure a routing session using standard IP Version 4 (IPv4) address prefixes, use the address-family ipv4 command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: address-family ipv6
commands.description: To enter address family to configure a routing session such as BGP that use using standard IP Version 6 (IPv6) address prefixes, use the address-family ipv6 command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: address-pool
commands.description: To specify a list of address pools for allocating addresses to remote clients, use the address-pool command in tunnel-group general-attributes configuration mode.

commands.name: address-pools
commands.description: To specify a list of address pools for allocating addresses to remote clients, use the address-pools command in group-policy attributes configuration mode.

commands.name: admin-context
commands.description: To set the admin context for the system configuration, use the admin-context command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: advertise passive-only
commands.description: To configure IS-IS to advertise only prefixes that belong to passive interfaces, use the advertise passive-only command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: aggregate-address
commands.syntax: aggregate-address address mask [as-set] [summary-only] [suppress-map map-name] [advertise-map map-name] [attribute-map map-name]
commands.description: To create an aggregate entry in a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) database, use the aggregate-address command in address family configuration mode.

commands.name: alarm contact description
commands.description: To enter a description for the alarm inputs in the ISA 3000, use the alarm contact description command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: alarm contact severity
commands.syntax: alarm contact {1 | 2 | all} severity {major | minor | none}
commands.description: To specify the severity of an alarm in the ISA 3000, use the alarm contact severity command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: alarm contact trigger
commands.description: To specify a trigger for one or all alarm inputs in the ISA 3000, use the alarm contact trigger command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: alarm facility input-alarm
commands.description: To specify the logging and notification options for alarm inputs in the ISA 3000, use the alarm facility input-alarm command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: alarm facility power-supply rps
commands.syntax: alarm facility power-supply rps {disable | notifies | relay | syslog}
commands.description: To configure power supply alarms in the ISA 3000, use the alarm facility power-supply rps command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: alarm facility temperature (actions)
commands.syntax: alarm facility temperature {primary | secondary} {notifies | relay | syslog}
commands.description: To configure the temperature alarms in the ISA 3000, use the alarm facility temperature command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: alarm facility temperature (high and low thresholds)
commands.commandTemplate: alarm facility temperature (high and low thresholds)
commands.syntax: alarm facility temperature {primary | secondary} {high | low} threshold
commands.description: To configure the high and low temperature threshold values in the ISA 3000, use the alarm facility temperature {low | high } command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: allocate-interface
commands.description: To allocate interfaces to a security context, use the allocate-interface command in context configuration mode.

commands.name: allocate-ips
commands.description: To allocate an IPS virtual sensor to a security context if you have the AIP SSM installed, use the allocate-ips command in context configuration mode.

commands.name: allow-ssc-mgmt
commands.description: To set an interface on the ASA 5505 to be the SSC management interface, use the allow-ssc-mgmt command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: allow-tls
commands.description: To configure ESMTP inspection to allow or prohibit TLS sessions, use the allow-tls command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: allowed-eid
commands.description: To configure a LISP inspection map to limit inspected EIDs based on IP address, use the allowed-eid command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: always-on-vpn
commands.description: To configure the behavior of the Secure Client Always-On-VPN functionality, use the always-on-vpn command in group policy configuration mode.

commands.name: anti-replay
commands.description: To enable anti-replay for GTP-U message sequence numbers, use the anti-replay command in GTP inspection policy map parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect ask
commands.syntax: anyconnect ask {none | enable [default {webvpn | anyconnect} timeout value]}
commands.description: To enable the ASA to prompt remote SSL VPN client users to download the client, use the anyconnect ask command in group policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration modes.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect df-bit-ignore
commands.description: To ignore the DF bit in packets that need fragmentation, use the anyconnect-df-bit-ignore command in group policy webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect dpd-interval
commands.description: To enable Dead Peer Detection (DPD) on the ASA and to set the frequency that either the remote client or the ASA performs DPD over SSL VPN connections, use the anyconnect dpd-interval command in group policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect dtls compression
commands.description: To enable compression on low bandwidth links for a specific group or user, use the Secure Client dtls compression command in group policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect enable
commands.description: To enable the ASA to download an Secure Client to remote computers or to connect to the ASA using the Secure Client with SSL or IKEv2, use the anyconnect enable command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect external-browser-pkg
commands.description: To configure the path for the Secure Client external browser package, use the anyconnect external-browser-pkg command in the webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect firewall-rule
commands.syntax: anyconnect firewall-rule client interface {public | private} ACL
commands.description: To establish a public or provide ACL firewall, use the anyconnect firewall-rule command in either group policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect image
commands.description: To install or upgrade the Secure Client distribution package and add it to the running configuration, use the anyconnect image command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect keep-installer
commands.description: Note
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect modules
commands.description: To specify the names of modules that the AnyConnect SSL VPN Client requires for optional features, use the anyconnect modules command in group policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect mtu
commands.description: To adjust the MTU size for VPN connections established by the Cisco AnyConnect VPN Client, use the anyconnect mtu command in group policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect profiles (group-policy attributes webvpn, username attributes webvpn)
commands.commandTemplate: anyconnect profiles (group-policy attributes webvpn, username attributes webvpn)
commands.description: To specify a CVC profiles package downloaded to Cisco AnyConnect VPN Client (CVC) users, use the anyconnect profiles command in webvpn or configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect profiles (webvpn)
commands.description: To specify a file as a profiles package that the ASA loads in cache memory and makes available to group policies and username attributes of Cisco AnyConnect VPN Client (CVC) users, use the anyconnect profiles command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect ssl compression
commands.description: To enable compression of http data over an SSL VPN connection for a specific group or user, use the anyconnect ssl compression command in group policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect ssl df-bit-ignore
commands.description: To enable the forced fragmentation of packets on an SSL VPN connection (allowing them to pass through the tunnel) for a specific group or user, use the anyconnect ssl df-bit-ignore command in the group policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect ssl dtls enable
commands.description: To enable Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) connections on an interface for specific groups or users establishing SSL VPN connections with the Cisco AnyConnect VPN Client, use the anyconnect ssl dtls enable command in group policy webvpn or username attributes webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect ssl keepalive
commands.description: To configure the frequency of keepalive messages which a remote client sends to the ASA over SSL VPN connections, use the anyconnect ssl keepalive command in group policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration modes.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect ssl rekey
commands.syntax: anyconnect ssl rekey {method {ssl | new-tunnel} | time minutes | none}
commands.description: To enable a remote client to perform a rekey on an SSL VPN connection, use the anyconnect ssl rekey command in group-policy webvpn or username webvpn configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group policy webvpn configuration, Username webvpn configuration

commands.name: anyconnect-custom (Version 9.0 through 9.2)
commands.description: To set or update the value of a custom attribute, use the anyconnect-custom command in anyconnect-custom-attr configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect-custom (Version 9.3 and later)
commands.description: To set or update the value of a custom attribute, use the anyconnect-custom command in group-policy or dynamic-access-policy-record configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect-custom-attr (Version 9.0 through 9.2)
commands.description: To create custom attributes, use the anyconnect-custom-attr command in Anyconnect-custom-attr configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect-custom-attr (Version 9.3 and later)
commands.description: To create custom attribute types, use the anyconnect-custom-attr command in config-webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect-custom-data
commands.description: To create custom attribute named values, use the anyconnect-custom-data command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: anyconnect-essentials
commands.description: To enable AnyConnect Essentials on the ASA, use the anyconnect-essentials command in group policy webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: apcf
commands.description: To enable an Application Profile Customization Framework profile, use the apcf command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: app-agent heartbeat
commands.description: To configure the heartbeat message interval for the app-agent (application agent) running on the ASA to check the health of the chassis, use the app-agent heartbeat command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: app-id
commands.description: The app-id command specifies the Cisco-defined application ID in a network-service object.

commands.name: appl-acl
commands.description: To identify a previously configured webtype ACL to apply to a session, use the appl-acl command in dap webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: application-access
commands.description: To customize the Application Access fields of the WebVPN Home page that is displayed to authenticated WebVPN users, and the Application Access window that is launched when the user selects an application, use the application-access command in customization configuration mode.

commands.name: application-access hide-details
commands.description: To hide application details that are displayed in the WebVPN Applications Access window, use the application-access hide-details command in customization configuration mode, which is accessed by using the webvpn command or the tunnel-group webvpn-attributes command.

commands.name: area
commands.description: To create an OSPF v2 or OSPFv3 area, use the area command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: area authentication
commands.description: To enable authentication for an OSPFv2 area, use the area authentication command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: area default-cost
commands.description: To specify a cost for the default summary route sent into a stub or NSSA, use the area default-cost command in router configuration mode or IPv6 router configuration mode.

commands.name: area filter-list prefix
commands.syntax: area area_id filter-list prefix list_name {in | out}
commands.description: To filter prefixes advertised in Type 3 LSAs between OSPFv2 areas of an ABR, use the area filter-list prefix command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: area nssa
commands.description: To configure an area as an NSSA, use the area nssa command in router configuration mode or IPv6 router configuration mode.

commands.name: area range (ipv6 router ospf)
commands.syntax: area area_id ipv6-prefix-/prefix-length [advertise | not advertise] [cost cost]
commands.description: To consolidate and summarize OSPFv3 routes at an area boundary, use the area range command in ipv6 router ospf configuration mode.

commands.name: area range (router ospf)
commands.syntax: area area_id range address mask advertise | not-advertise]
commands.description: To consolidate and summarize routes at an area boundary, use the area range command in router ospf configuration mode.

commands.name: area stub
commands.description: To define an area as a stub area, use the area stub command in router configuration mode or IPv6 router configuration mode.

commands.name: area virtual-link (ipv6 router ospf)
commands.syntax: area area_id virtual-link router_id [hello-interval seconds] [retransmit-interval seconds] [transmit-delay seconds] [dead-interval seconds] [ttl-security hops hop-count]
commands.description: To define an OSPFv3 virtual link, use the area virtual-link command in ipv6 router ospf configuration mode.

commands.name: area virtual-link (router ospf)
commands.syntax: area area_id virtual-link router_id [authentication [key-chain key-chain-name | message-digest | null]] [hello-interval seconds] [retransmit-interval seconds] [dead-interval seconds [[[[authentication-key[0 | 8] key] | [message-digest-key key_id md5[0 | 8] key]]]]
commands.description: To define an OSPF virtual link, use the area virtual-link command in router ospf configuration mode.

commands.name: area-password
commands.description: To configure the IS-IS area authentication password, use the area-password command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: arp
commands.description: To add a static ARP entry to the ARP table, use the arp command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: arp permit-nonconnected
commands.description: To enable the ARP cache to also include non-directly-connected subnets, use the arp permit-nonconnected command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: arp rate-limit
commands.description: To set the ARP rate limit to control the number of ARP packets per second, use the arp rate-limit command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: arp timeout
commands.description: To set the time before the ASA rebuilds the ARP table, use the arp timeout command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: arp-inspection
commands.description: To enable ARP inspection for transparent firewall mode, use the arp-inspection command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: as-path access-list
commands.description: To configure an autonomous system path filter using a regular expression, use the as-path access-list command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: asdm disconnect
commands.description: To terminate an active ASDM session, use the asdm disconnect command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: asdm disconnect log_session
commands.description: To terminate an active ASDM logging session, use the asdm disconnect log_session command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: asdm history enable
commands.description: To enable ASDM history tracking, use the asdm history enable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: asdm image
commands.description: To specify the location of the ASDM software image in flash memory, use the asdm image command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: asdm location
commands.description: Caution

commands.name: asp load-balance per-packet
commands.description: For multi-core ASAs, to change the load balancing behavior to be per packet, use the asp load-balance per-packet command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: asp rule-engine compile-offload
commands.description: Use the asp rule-engine compile-offload command to enable or disable the compile offload function for the rule engine.

commands.name: asp rule-engine transactional-commit
commands.description: Use the asp rule-engine transactional-commit command to enable or disable the transactional commit model for the rule engine.

commands.name: asr-group
commands.description: To specify an asymmetrical routing interface group ID, use the asr-group command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: assertion-consumer-url
commands.description: Note

commands.name: attribute bind
commands.syntax: attribute bind agent-name binding ip-address type attribute-type value attribute-value
commands.description: To change the IP-to-attribute binding for an attribute-based network object, use the attribute bind command in EXEC mode.

commands.name: attribute source-group
commands.description: To configure a VM attribute agent to communicate with VMware vCenter or a single ESXi host, use the attribute source-group command in EXEC mode.

commands.name: attribute source-group host
commands.syntax: host ip-address username ESXi-username password ESXi-password
commands.description: To configure VMware vCenter host credentials that allow a VM attribute agent to communicate with vCenter or a single ESXi host, use the attribute source-group host command in attribute agent configuration mode.

commands.name: attribute source-group keepalive
commands.description: To configure keepalive settings for VMware vCenter communication, use the attribute source-group keepalive command in attribute agent configuration mode.

commands.name: attributes
commands.description: To specify attribute value pairs that the ASA writes to the DAP attribute database, enter the attributes command in dap test attributes mode.

commands.name: auth-cookie-name
commands.description: To specify the name of an authentication cookie, use the auth-cookie-name command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: auth-prompt
commands.description: To specify or change the AAA challenge text for through-the-ASA user sessions, use the auth-prompt command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: authenticated-session-username
commands.description: To specify which authentication username to associate with the session when double authentication is enabled, use the authenticated-session-username command in tunnel-group general-attributes mode.

commands.name: authentication
commands.description: To configure the authentication method for WebVPN and e-mail proxies, use the authentication command in various modes.
commands.mode: Imap4s configuration, Pop3s configuration, Smtps configuration, Webvpn configuration, Tunnel group Webvpn configuration

commands.name: authentication (bfd-template)
commands.description: To configure authentication in a BFD template for single-hop and multi-hop sessions, use the authentication command in BFD configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication eap-proxy
commands.description: For L2TP over IPsec connections, to enable EAP and permit the ASA to proxy the PPP authentication process to an external RADIUS authentication server, use the authentication eap-proxy command in tunnel-group ppp-attributes configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication key
commands.description: To enable authentication for IS-IS, use the authentication key command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication key eigrp
commands.syntax: authentication key eigrp as-number key key-id key-id
commands.description: To enable authentication of EIGRP packets and specify the authentication key, use the authentication key eigrp command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication mode
commands.description: To specify the type of authentication used in IS-IS packets for the IS-IS instance, use the authentication mode command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication ms-chap-v1
commands.description: For L2TP over IPsec connections, to enable Microsoft CHAP, Version 1 authentication for PPP, use the authentication ms-chap-v1 command in tunnel-group ppp-attributes configuration mode.To return the command to its default setting (permit CHAP and MS-CHAP), use the no form of this command.

commands.name: authentication ms-chap-v2
commands.description: For L2TP over IPsec connections, to enable Microsoft CHAP, Version 2 authentication for PPP, use the authentication ms-chap-v1 command in tunnel-group ppp-attributes configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication pap
commands.description: For L2TP over IPsec connections, to permit PAP authentication for PPP, use the authentication pap command in tunnel-group ppp-attributes configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication send-only
commands.description: To specify for the IS-IS instance that authentication is performed only on IS-IS packets being sent (not received), use the authentication send-only command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication-attr-from-server
commands.description: To specify which authentication server authorization attributes to apply to the connection when double authentication is enabled, use the authentication-attr-from-server command in tunnel-group general-attributes mode.

commands.name: authentication-certificate
commands.description: To request a certificate from a WebVPN client establishing a connection, use the authentication-certificate command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication-exclude
commands.description: To enable end users to browse to configured links without logging in to clientless SSL VPN, enter the authentication-exclude command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication-port
commands.description: To specify the port number used for RADIUS authentication for this host, use the authentication-port command in aaa-server configuration host configuration mode.

commands.name: authentication-server-group (imap4s, pop3s, smtps)
commands.description: Note
commands.mode: Imap4s configuration, Pop3s configuration, Smtps configuration

commands.name: authentication-server-group (tunnel-group general-attributes)
commands.description: To specify the AAA server group to use for user authentication for a tunnel group, use the authentication-server-group command in tunnel-group general-attributes configuration mode.

commands.name: authorization-required
commands.description: To require users to authorize successfully prior to connecting, use the authorization-required command in various modes.
commands.mode: Imap4s configuration, Pop3s configuration, Smtps configuration, Tunnel-group general-attributes configuration

commands.name: authorization-server-group (imap4s, pop3s, smtps)
commands.description: Note
commands.mode: Imap4s configuration, Pop3s configuration, Smtps configuration

commands.name: authorization-server-group (tunnel-group general-attributes)
commands.description: To specify the set of authorization servers to use for a tunnel group for all remote access VPNs, use the authorization-server-group command in various modes.

commands.name: authorize-only
commands.description: To enable authorize-only mode for a RADIUS AAA server group, use the authorize-only command in aaa-server group configuration mode.

commands.name: auto-signon
commands.syntax: auto-signon allow {ip ip-address ip-mask | uri resource-mask} auth-type {basic | ftp | ntlm | all}
commands.description: To configure the ASA to automatically pass user login credentials for clientless SSL VPN connections on to internal servers, use the auto-signon command in any of three modes: webvpn configuration, webvpn group configuration, or webvpn username configuration mode.
commands.mode: Webvpn configuration (global), Webvpn group policy configuration, Webvpn username configuration

commands.name: auto-summary
commands.description: To enable the automatic summarization of subnet routes into network-level routes, use the auto-summary command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: auto-update device-id
commands.syntax: auto-update device-id [hardware-serial | hostname | ipaddress | [if_name] | mac-address [if_name] | string text]
commands.description: To configure the ASA device ID for use with an Auto Update Server, use the auto-update device-id command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: auto-update poll-at
commands.description: To schedule a specific time for the ASA to poll the Auto Update Server, use the auto-update poll-at command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: auto-update poll-period
commands.description: To configure how often the ASA checks for updates from an Auto Update Server, use the auto-update poll-period command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: auto-update server
commands.description: To identify the Auto Update Server, use the auto-update server command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: auto-update timeout
commands.description: To set a timeout period in which to contact the Auto Update Server, use the auto-update timeout command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: avc
commands.description: To enable Application Visibility Control (AVC) and download the Vulnerability Database (VDB), use the avc command in global configuration mode.
commands.mode: Global configuration Privileged EXEC mode for download
modes: Global configuration Privileged EXEC mode for download

commands.name: backup
commands.description: To back up an ASA configuration, certificates, keys, and images, use the backup command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: backup interface
commands.description: For models with a built-in switch, such as the ASA 5505, use the backup interface command in interface configuration mode to identify a VLAN interface as a backup interface, for example, to an ISP.

commands.name: backup-package auto
commands.description: To configure automatic backup and restore operations on a Cisco ISA 3000, use the backup-package auto command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: backup-package location
commands.syntax: backup-package {backup | restore} [interface name] location disk n: [passphrase string
commands.description: To configure the backup and restore locations to be used in subsequent backup and restore operations on a Cisco ISA 3000, use the backup-package location command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: backup-servers
commands.description: To configure backup servers, use the backup-servers command in group-policy configuration mode.

commands.name: banner (global)
commands.description: To configure the ASDM, session, login, or message-of-the-day banner, use the banner command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: banner (group-policy)
commands.description: To display a banner or welcome text on remote clients when they connect, use the banner command in group-policy configuration mode.

commands.name: base-url
commands.description: (Optional) Configures the base URL of the Clientless VPN.

commands.name: basic-mapping-rule
commands.description: To configure the basic mapping rule in a Mapping Address and Port (MAP) domain, use the basic-mapping-rule command in MAP domain configuration mode.

commands.name: basic-security
commands.description: To define an action when the Security (SEC) option occurs in a packet header with IP Options inspection, use the basic-security command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: bfd echo
commands.description: To enable BFD echo mode on the interface, use the bfd echo command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: bfd interval
commands.syntax: bfd interval milliseconds min_rx milliseconds multiplier multiplier-value
commands.description: To configure the baseline BFD parameters on the interface, use the bfd command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: bfd map
commands.syntax: bfd map {ipv4 | ipv6} destination/cdir source/cdir template-name
commands.description: To configure a BFD map that associates addresses with multi-hop templates, use the bfd map command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: bfd slow-timers
commands.description: To configure the BFD slow timers value, use the bfd slow-timers command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: bfd-template
commands.description: To configure the BFD template and enter BFD configuration mode, use the bfd-template command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp aggregate-timer
commands.description: To set the interval at which BGP routes will be aggregated or to disable timer-based route aggregation, use the bgp aggregate-timer command in address family configuration mode.
commands.mode: Address-family configuration, Address-family IPv6 sub mode
modes: Address-family configuration, Address-family IPv6 sub mode

commands.name: bgp always-compare-med
commands.description: To enable the comparison of the Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) for paths from neighbors in different autonomous systems, use the bgp always-compare-med command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp asnotation dot
commands.description: To change the default display and regular expression match format of Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) 4-byte autonomous system numbers from asplain (decimal values) to dot notation, use the bgp asnotation dot command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp bestpath compare-routerid
commands.description: To configure a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routing process to compare identical routes received from different external peers during the best path selection process and to select the route with the lowest router ID as the best path, use the bgp bestpath compare-routerid command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp bestpath med missing-as-worst
commands.description: To configure a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routing process to assign a value of infinity to routes that are missing the Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) attribute (making the path without a MED value the least desirable path), use the bgp bestpath med missing-as-worst command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp default local-preference
commands.description: To change the default local preference value, use the bgp default local-preference command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp deterministic-med
commands.description: To enforce the deterministic comparison of the Multi Exit Discriminator (MED) value between all paths received from within the same autonomous system use the bgp deterministic-med command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp enforce-first-as
commands.description: To configures an ASA to deny an update received from an external BGP (eBGP) peer that does not list its autonomous system number at the beginning of the AS_PATH in the incoming update, use the bgp enforce-first-as command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp fast-external-fallover
commands.description: To configure a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routing process to immediately reset external BGP peering sessions if the link used to reach these peers goes down, use the bgp fast-external-fallover command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp graceful-restart
commands.description: To configure a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routing process for graceful restart in a non-stop forwarding configuration, use the bgp graceful-restart command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp inject-map
commands.description: To configure conditional route injection to inject more specific routes into a Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routing table, use the bgp inject-map command in address family configuration mode.
commands.mode: Address-family configuration, Address-family IPv6 sub mode
modes: Address-family configuration, Address-family IPv6 sub mode

commands.name: bgp log-neighbor-changes
commands.description: To enable logging of BGP neighbor resets, use the bgp log-neighbor-changes command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp maxas-limit
commands.description: To configure Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) to discard routes that has a number of autonomous system numbers in AS-path that exceed the specified value, use the bgp maxas-limit command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp nexthop
commands.syntax: bgp nexthop {trigger {delay seconds | enable} | route-map map-name}
commands.description: To configure Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) next-hop address tracking, use the bgp nexthop command in address family or router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp redistribute-internal
commands.description: To configure iBGP redistribution into an interior gateway protocol (IGP), such as EIGRP or OSPF, use the bgp redistribute-internal command in address family configuration mode.
commands.mode: Address-family configuration Address-family IPv6 sub mode
modes: Address-family configuration Address-family IPv6 sub mode

commands.name: bgp router-id
commands.description: To configure a fixed router ID for the local Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routing process, use the bgp router-id command in address family router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp scan-time
commands.description: To configure scanning intervals of Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) routers for next hop validation use the bgp scan-time command in address family configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp suppress-inactive
commands.description: To suppress the advertisement of routes that are not installed in the routing information base (RIB), use the bgp suppress-inactive command in address family or router configuration mode.
commands.mode: Address family configuration Address family IPv6 sub-mode
modes: Address family configuration Address family IPv6 sub-mode

commands.name: bgp transport
commands.description: To enable TCP transport session parameters globally for all Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) sessions, use the bgp transport command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: bgp-community new-format
commands.description: To configure BGP to display communities in the format AA:NN (autonomous system:community number/4-byte number), use the bgp-community new-format command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: blocks
commands.description: To allocate additional memory to block diagnostics (displayed by the show blocks command), use the blocks command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: boot
commands.description: To specify which image the system uses at the next reload and which configuration file the system uses at startup, use the boot command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: border style
commands.description: To customize the border of the WebVPN Home page that is displayed to authenticated WebVPN users, use the border style command in customization configuration mode.

commands.name: breakout
commands.description: To break out 10GB ports from a 40GB or higher interface, use the breakout command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: bridge-group
commands.description: To assign an interface to a bridge group, use the bridge-group command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: browse-networks
commands.description: To customize the Browse Networks box of the WebVPN Home page that is displayed to authenticated WebVPN users, use the browse-networks command in webvpn customization configuration mode.

commands.name: ca-check
commands.description: To configure the basic constraints extension and set the CA flag in a trustpoint certificate, use the ca-check command in crypto ca trustpoint configuration mode.

commands.name: cache
commands.description: To enter cache mode and set values for caching attributes, enter the cache command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: cache-static-content
commands.description: To cache all static content used for Clientless SSL VPN connections, enter the cache-static-content command in webvpn cache configuration mode.

commands.name: cache-time
commands.description: To specify in minutes how long to allow a CRL to remain in the cache before considering it stale, use the cache-time command in ca-crl configuration mode, which is accessible from crypto ca trustpoint configuration mode.

commands.name: call-agent
commands.description: To specify a group of call agents, use the call-agent command in mgcp map configuration mode.

commands.name: call-duration-limit
commands.description: To configure the call duration for an H.323 call, use the call-duration-limit command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: call-home
commands.description: To enter call home configuration mode, use the call-home command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: call-home send
commands.syntax: call-home send cli command [email email] [service-number service number]
commands.description: To execute a CLI command and e-mail the command output to a specified address, use the call-home send command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: call-home send alert-group
commands.syntax: call-home send alert-group {configuration | telemetry | inventory | group snapshot} [profile profile-name]
commands.description: To send a specific alert group message, use the call-home send alert-group command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: call-home test
commands.description: To manually send a Call Home test message using the configuration of a profile, use the call-home test command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: call-party-numbers
commands.description: To enforce sending call party numbers during an H.323 call setup, use the call-party-numbers command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: capability lls
commands.description: The LLS capability is enabled by default.

commands.name: capability opaque
commands.description: To enable Multiprotocol Label Switching traffic engineering (MPLS TE) topology information to flood the network through opaque LSAs, use the capability opaque command in the router-configuration mode.

commands.name: captive-portal
commands.description: To enable captive portal for the ASA FirePOWER module, use the captive-portal command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: capture
commands.syntax: capture capture_name [type {asp-drop [all | drop-code] | tls-proxy | raw-data | isakmp [ikev1 | ikev2] | inline-tag [tag] | webvpn user webvpn-user}] [access-list access_list_name {interface {interface_name | asa_dataplane asa_mgmt_plane | cplane}} [buffer buf_size] [ethernet-type type] [reeinject-hide] [packet-length bytes] [circular-buffer] [trace [trace-count number]] [real-time [dump] [detail]] [match protocol {host source-ip | source-ip mask | any | any4 | any6} [operator src_port] {host dest_ip | dest_ip mask |  | any | any4 | any6} [operator dest_port]] [switch] [offload] [ivlan number] [ovlan number]
commands.description: To enable packet capture capabilities for packet sniffing and network fault isolation, use the capture command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: cd
commands.description: To change the current working directory to the one specified, use the cd command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: cdp-url
commands.description: To specify the CDP to be included in certificates issued by the local CA, use the cdp-url command in ca server configuration mode.

commands.name: certificate
commands.description: To add the indicated certificate, use the certificate command in crypto ca certificate chain configuration mode.

commands.name: certificate-group-map
commands.description: To associate a rule entry from a certificate map with a tunnel group, use the certificate-group-map command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: chain
commands.description: To enable sending a certificate chain, use the chain command in tunnel-group ipsec-attributes configuration mode.

commands.name: change-password
commands.description: To enable users to change their own account passwords, use the change-password command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: changeto
commands.description: To change between security contexts and the system, use the changeto command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: channel-group
commands.description: To assign a physical interface to an EtherChannel, use the channel-group command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: character-encoding
commands.description: To specify the global character encoding in WebVPN portal pages, use the character-encoding command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: check-retransmission
commands.description: To prevent against TCP retransmission style attacks, use the check-retransmission command in tcp-map configuration mode.

commands.name: checkheaps
commands.description: To configure checkheaps verification intervals, use the checkheaps command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: checksum-verification
commands.description: To enable or disable TCP checksum verification, use the checksum-verification command in tcp-map configuration mode.

commands.name: cipc security-mode authenticated
commands.description: To force Cisco IP Communicator (CIPC) softphones to operate in authenticated mode when CIPC softphones are deployed in a voice and data VLAN scenario, use the cipc security-mode authenticated command in phone-proxy configuration mode.

commands.name: clacp static-port-priority
commands.description: To disable dynamic port priority in LACP for a clustering spanned EtherChannel, which is required for more than 8 active EtherChannel members, use the clacp static-port-priority command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: clacp system-mac
commands.description: To manually configure the cLACP system ID on the master unit in an ASA cluster, use the clacp system-mac command in cluster group configuration mode.

commands.name: class (global)
commands.description: To create a resource class to which to assign a security context, use the class command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: class (policy-map)
commands.description: To assign a class map to a policy map where you can assign actions to the class map traffic, use the class command in policy-map configuration mode.

commands.name: class-map
commands.description: When using the Modular Policy Framework, identify Layer 3 or 4 traffic to which you want to apply actions by using the class-map command (without the type keyword) in global configuration mode.

commands.name: class-map type inspect
commands.syntax: class-map type inspect application [match-all | match-any] class_map_name
commands.description: When using the Modular Policy Framework, match criteria that is specific to an inspection application by using the class-map type inspect command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: class-map type management
commands.description: When using the Modular Policy Framework, identify Layer 3 or 4 management traffic destined for the ASA to which you want to apply actions by using the class-map type management command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: class-map type regex
commands.description: When using the Modular Policy Framework, group regular expressions for use with matching text by using the class-map type regex command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: clear aaa kerberos
commands.description: To clear Kerberos information, use the clear aaa kerberos command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear aaa local user
commands.syntax: clear aaa local user {fail-attempts | lockout} {username name | all}
commands.description: To unlock a user, or to reset a user’s failed authentication attempts to zero, use the clear aaa local user command in Privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear aaa sdi node-secret
commands.description: To delete the node secret file for an RSA SecurID server, use the clear aaa sdi node-secret command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear aaa-server statistics
commands.syntax: clear aaa-server statistics [LOCAL | groupname [host hostname] | protocol protocol]
commands.description: To reset the statistics for AAA servers, use the clear aaa-server statistics command in privilged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear access-list
commands.description: To clear an access-list counter, use the clear access-list command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: clear arp
commands.description: To clear dynamic ARP entries or ARP statistics, use the clear arp command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear asp
commands.syntax: clear asp {cluster counter | drop [flow | frame] | event dp-cp | queue-exhaustion [snapshot number] | load-balance history | overhead | table [arp | classify | network-object | filter [access-list acl_name]]}
commands.description: To clear accelerated security path (ASP) statistics, use the clear asp command.

commands.name: clear avc
commands.description: To clear statistics and hit counts for the Application Visibility and Control (AVC) feature, use the clear avc command in Privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear bfd counters
commands.syntax: clear bfd counters [ld local_discr | interface_name | ipv4 ip-address | ipv6 ipv6-address]
commands.description: To clear the BFD counters, use the clear bfd counters command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear bgp
commands.syntax: clear bgp {[* | external] [ipv4 unicast [as_number | neighbor_address | table-map] | ipv6 unicast [as_number | neighbor_address]] [soft] [in | out] | as_number [soft] [in | out] | neighbor_address [soft] [in | out] | table-map}
commands.description: Note

commands.name: clear blocks
commands.description: To reset the packet buffer counters such as the exhaustion condition and history information, use the clear blocks command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear capture
commands.description: To clear the capture buffer, use the clear capture command in privileged EXEC configuration mode.

commands.name: clear clns cache
commands.description: To clear and reinitialize the Connectionless Network Service (CLNS) routing cache, use the clear clns cache EXEC command.

commands.name: clear clns is-neighbors
commands.description: To remove IS neighbor information from the adjacency database, use the clear clns is-neighbors EXEC command.

commands.name: clear clns neighbors
commands.description: To remove CLNS neighbor information from the adjacency database, use the clear clns neighbors EXEC command.

commands.name: clear clns route
commands.description: To remove all of the dynamically derived CLNS routing information, use the clear clns route EXEC command.

commands.name: clear cluster info
commands.syntax: clear cluster info {flow-mobility counters | health details | trace | transport}
commands.description: To clear cluster statistics, use the clear cluster info command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear compression
commands.description: To clear compression statistics for all SVC and WebVPN connections, use the clear compression command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear configuration session
commands.description: To delete a configuration session, use the clear configuration session command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: clear configure
commands.description: To clear the running configuration, use the clear configure command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: clear conn
commands.syntax: clear conn [all] [tcp | udp | sctp}] [address src_ip] [- src_ip] [netmask mask]] [port src_port [- src_port]] [address dest_ip [- dest_ip] [netmask mask]] [port dest_port [- dest_port] [user [domain_nickname\] user_name | user-group [domain_nickname\\] user_group_name] | zone [zone_name]] [data-rate]
commands.description: To clear a specific connection or multiple connections, use the clear conn command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear console-output
commands.description: To remove the currently captured console output, use the clear console-output command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear coredump
commands.description: To clear the coredump log, use the clear coredump command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: clear counters
commands.syntax: clear counters [all | context context-name | summary | top n] [detail] [protocol protocol_name | counter_name]] [threshold n]
commands.description: To clear the protocol stack counters, use the clear counters command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: clear cpu profile
commands.description: To clear the CPU profiling statistics, use the clear cpu profile command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crashinfo
commands.description: To delete all the crash information files stored in flash memory, use the clear crashinfo command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto accelerator statistics
commands.description: To clear the the global and accelerator-specific statistics from the crypto accelerator MIB, use the clear crypto accelerator statistics command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto ca crls
commands.syntax: clear crypto ca crls [trustpoool | trustpoint trust_point_name]
commands.description: To empty the CRL cache of all CRLs associated with a specified trustpoint, all CRLs associated with the trustpool from the cache, or the CRL cache of all CRLs, use the clear crypto ca crls command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto ca trustpool
commands.description: To remove all certificates from the trustpool, use the clear crypto ca trustpool command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto ikev1
commands.description: To remove the IPsec IKEv1 SAs or statistics, use the clear crypto ikev1 command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto ikev2
commands.description: To remove the IPsec IKEv2 SAs or statistics, use the clear crypto ikev2 command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto ipsec sa
commands.syntax: clear crypto ipsec sa [counters | entry ip_address {esp | ah} spi | map map name | peer ip_address]
commands.description: To remove the IPsec SA counters, entries, crypto maps or peer connections, use the clear crypto ipsec sa command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto ipsec stats
commands.description: To remove the global IPsec statistics and reset the statistics, use the clear crypto ipsec stats command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto isakmp
commands.description: To clear ISAKMP SAs or statistics, use the clear crypto isakmp command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto protocol statistics
commands.description: To clear the protocol-specific statistics in the crypto accelerator MIB, use the clear crypto protocol statistics command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear crypto ssl
commands.syntax: clear crypto ssl {cache [all] | errors | mib | objects}
commands.description: To clear SSL information, use the clear crypto ssl command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear cts
commands.description: To clear data used by the ASA when integrated with Cisco TrustSec, use the clear cts command in global configuration mode:

commands.name: clear dhcpd
commands.description: To clear the DHCP server bindings and statistics, use the clear dhcp command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear dhcprelay statistics
commands.description: To clear the DHCP relay statistic counters, use the clear dhcprelay statistics command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear dns
commands.description: To clear IP addresses associated with fully qualified domain name (FQDN) hosts, use the clear dns command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear dns-hosts cache
commands.description: To clear the DNS cache, use the clear dns-hosts cache command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear dynamic-filter dns-snoop
commands.description: To clear Botnet Traffic Filter DNS snooping data, use the clear dynamic-filter dns-snoop command in in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear dynamic-filter reports
commands.syntax: clear dynamic-filter reports {top [malware-sites | malware-ports | infected-hosts] | infected-hosts}
commands.description: To clear report data for the Botnet Traffic Filter, use the clear dynamic-filter reports command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear dynamic-filter statistics
commands.description: To clear Botnet Traffic Filter statistics, use the clear dynamic-filter statistics command in in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear eigrp events
commands.description: To clear the EIGRP event log, use the clear eigrp events command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear eigrp neighbors
commands.description: To delete entries from the EIGRP neighbor table, use the clear eigrp neighbors command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear eigrp topology
commands.description: To delete entries from the EIGRP topology table, use the clear eigrp topology command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear facility-alarm output
commands.description: To de-energize the output relay and clear the alarm state of the LED in the ISA 3000, use the clear facility-alarm output command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear failover statistics
commands.description: To clear the failover statistic counters, use the clear failover statistics command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear flow-export counters
commands.description: To reset runtime counters for NetFlow statistical and error data to zero, use the clear flow-export counters command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: clear flow-offload
