commands.description: To configure the public cloud failover peer, use the failover cloud peer command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover cloud polltime
commands.description: To specify the public cloud failover unit poll and hold times, use the failover cloud polltime command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover cloud port
commands.syntax: failover cloud port {control port-number | probe port-number [interface if-name]}
commands.description: To specify the two TCP ports used by public cloud failover pairs, the port used for failover communication between the two peers, and the port used for Azure Load Balancer probes, use the failover cloud port command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover cloud route-table
commands.description: To configure an Azure route table that directs internal routes to the Active unit, use the failover cloud route-table command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover cloud route-table rg
commands.description: To configure an Azure resource group, required for route table update requests, use the rg command in cfg-fover-cloud-rt configuration mode.

commands.name: failover cloud route-table route
commands.syntax: route {name route-name prefix address-prefix nexthop ip-address}
commands.description: To configure an route that requires updating during a failover, use the route command in cfg-fover-cloud-rt configuration mode.

commands.name: failover cloud subscription-id
commands.description: To configure the Azure Subscription ID for the Azure Service Principal, use the failover cloud subscription-id command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover cloud unit
commands.description: To configure the ASA Virtual as either the primary or secondary unit in a public cloud failover configuration, use the failover lan unit command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover exec
commands.description: To execute a command on a specific unit in a failover pair, use the failover exec command in privileged EXEC or global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover group
commands.description: To configure an Active/Active failover group, use the failover group command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover health-check bfd
commands.description: To configure Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) for unit health monitoring, use the failover health-check bfd command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover interface ip
commands.syntax: failover interface ip if_name [ip_address mask standby ip_address | ipv6_address | prefix standby ipv6_address]
commands.description: To specify the IPv4 address and mask or IPv6 address and prefixfor the failover interface and the Stateful Failover interface, use the failover interface ip command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover interface-policy
commands.description: To specify the policy for failover when monitoring detects an interface failure, use the failover interface-policy command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover ipsec pre-shared-key
commands.description: To establish IPsec LAN-to-LAN tunnels on the failover and state links between the units to encrypt all failover communications, use the failover ipsec pre-shared-key command in global configuration mode To remove the key, use the no form of this command.

commands.name: failover key
commands.description: To specify the key for encrypted and authenticated communication between units in a failover pair (over the failover and state links), use the failover key command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover lan interface
commands.description: To specify the interface used for failover communication, use the failover lan interface command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover lan unit
commands.description: To configure the ASA as either the primary or secondary unit in a LAN failover configuration, use the failover lan unit command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover link
commands.description: To specify the Stateful Failover interface and to enable Stateful Failover, use the failover link command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover mac address
commands.syntax: failover mac address phy_if active_mac standby_mac
commands.description: To specify the failover virtual MAC address for a physical interface, use the failover mac address command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover poll-time link-state
commands.description: To change the interface link state poll time, use the failover polltime link-state command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover polltime
commands.description: To specify the failover unit poll and hold times, use the failover polltime command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover polltime interface
commands.description: To specify the data interface polltime and holdtime in an Active/Standby failover configuration, use the failover polltime interface command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover reload-standby
commands.description: To force the standby unit to reboot, use the failover reload-standby command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: failover replication http
commands.description: To enable HTTP (port 80) connection replication, use the failover replication http command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover replication rate
commands.description: To configure the bulk-sync connection replication rate, use the failover replication rate command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover reset
commands.description: To restore a failed ASA to an unfailed state, use the failover reset command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: failover standby config-lock
commands.description: To lock configuration changes on the standby unit or standby context in a failover pair, use the failover standby config-lock command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover timeout
commands.description: To specify the failover reconnect timeout value for asymmetrically routed sessions, use the failover timeout command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: failover trace
commands.description: To configure and view trace levels of a failover trace log, use the failover trace command in configuration mode.

commands.name: failover wait-disable
commands.description: When using bridge groups or IPv6 duplicate address detection (DAD), to disable waiting for the failover peer unit to go into the standby state, use the failover wait-disable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: fallback
commands.syntax: fallback {sensitivity-file filename | monitoring timer timer_millisec hold-down timer timer_sec}
commands.description: To configure the fallback timers that the Cisco Intercompany Media Engine uses to fallback from VoIP to PSTN when connection integrity degrades, use the fallback command in uc-ime configuration mode.

commands.name: fast-flood
commands.description: To fill IS-IS link-state packets (LSPs), use the fast-flood command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: fault-monitor block-depletion
commands.description: To enable block depletion monitoring, enter the fault-monitor block depletion command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: fault-monitor mbuf-depletion
commands.description: To enable MBUF depletion monitoring, enter the fault-monitor mbuf-depletion command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: feature
commands.syntax: feature {tier standard | strong-encryption | context number | mobile-sp | carrier}
commands.description: To request smart licensing feature entitlements, use the feature command in license smart configuration mode.

commands.name: fec
commands.description: To set Forward Error Correction (FEC) for 25 Gbps and higher interfaces, use the fec command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: file-bookmarks
commands.syntax: file-bookmarks {link {style value} | title {style value | text value}}
commands.description: To customize the File Bookmarks title or the File Bookmarks links on the WebVPN Home page that is displayed to authenticated WebVPN users, use the file-bookmarks command from webvpn customization configuration mode.

commands.name: file-browsing
commands.description: To enable or disable CIFS/FTP file browsing for file servers or shares, use the file-browsing command in dap webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: file-encoding
commands.description: To specify the character encoding for pages from Common Internet File System servers, use the file-encoding command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: file-entry
commands.description: To enable or disable the ability of a user to enter file server names to access, use the file-entry command in dap webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: filter
commands.description: To specify the name of the access list to use for WebVPN connections for this group policy or username, use the filter command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: filter activex
commands.syntax: filter activex port [-port] | except local_ip mask foreign_ip foreign_mask
commands.description: To remove ActiveX objects in HTTP traffic passing through the ASA, use the filter activex command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: filter ftp
commands.syntax: filter ftp port [-port] except local_ip mask foreign_ip foreign_mask [allow] [interact-block]
commands.description: To identify the FTP traffic to be filtered by a Websense or N2H2 server, use the filter ftp command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: filter https
commands.syntax: filter https port [-port] | except local_ip mask foreign_ip [allow]
commands.description: To identify the HTTPS traffic to be filtered by a N2H2 or Websense server, use the filter https command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: filter java
commands.syntax: filter java {[port [- port] | except} local_ip local_mask foreign_ip foreign_mask]
commands.description: To remove Java applets from HTTP traffic passing through the ASA, use the filter java command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: filter url
commands.syntax: filter url port [- port] | except local_ip local_mask foreign_ip foreign_mask [allow] [cgi-truncate] [longurl-truncate | longurl-deny] [proxy-block]
commands.description: To direct traffic to a URL filtering server, use the filter url command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: fips enable
commands.description: To enable policy checking to enforce FIPS compliance on the system or module, use the fips enable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: fips self-test poweron
commands.description: To execute power-on self-tests, use the fips self-test powereon command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: firewall transparent
commands.description: To set the firewall mode to transparent mode, use the firewall transparent command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: flow-export active refresh-interval
commands.description: To specify the time interval between flow-update events, use the flow-export active refresh-interval command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: flow-export delay flow-create
commands.description: To delay export of the flow-create event, use the flow-export delay flow-create command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: flow-export destination
commands.syntax: flow-export destination interface-name ipv4-address | hostname udp-port
commands.description: To configure a collector to which NetFlow packets are sent, use the flow-export destination command in global configuration mode.

commands.syntax: flow-export event-type {all | flow-create | flow-denied | flow-update | flow-teardown} destination
commands.description: To configure the address of NetFlow collectors and filters to determine which NetFlow records should be sent to each collector, use the flow-export event-type destination command in policy-map class configuration mode.

commands.name: flow-export template timeout-rate
commands.description: To control the interval at which the template information is sent to NetFlow collectors, use the flow-export template timeout-rate command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: flow-mobility lisp
commands.description: To enable flow mobility for the cluster, use the flow-mobility lisp command in cluster configuration mode.

commands.name: flow-offload cluster-redirect
commands.description: To enable cluster redirect on the Secure Firewall 4200, use the flow-offload cluster-redirect command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: flow-offload enable

commands.name: flow-offload-dtls
commands.description: To enable DTLS crypto acceleration on the device, use the flow-offload-dtls command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: flow-offload-dtls egress-optimization
commands.description: To enable optimization of egress encrypted packets and improve latency, use the flow-offload-dtls egress-optimization command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: flow-offload-ipsec
commands.description: To enable IPsec flow off-loading, use the flow-offload-ipsec command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: flowcontrol
commands.description: To enable pause (XOFF) frames for flow control, use the flowcontrol command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: force re-authentication
commands.description: To allow an identity provider to authenticate directly rather than rely on a previous security context when a SAML authentication request occurs, use the force re-authentication command in saml idp webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: format
commands.description: To erase all files and format the file system, use the format command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: forward interface
commands.description: For models with a built-in switch, such as the ASA 5505, use the forward interface command in interface configuration mode to restore connectivity for one VLAN from initiating contact to one other VLAN.

commands.name: forward-reference
commands.description: To make it possible to refer to ACLs and objects that do not yet exist, use the forward-reference command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: fqdn (crypto ca trustpoint)

commands.name: fqdn (network object)
commands.description: To configure a FQDN for a network object, use the fqdn command in object configuration mode.

commands.name: fragment

commands.description: To provide additional management of packet fragmentation and improve compatibility with NFS, use the fragment command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: frequency
commands.description: To set the rate at which the selected SLA operation repeats, use the frequency command in SLA monitor protocol configuration mode.

commands.name: fsck
commands.description: To perform a file system check and to repair corruptions, use the fsck command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: ftp mode passive
commands.description: To set the FTP mode to passive, use the ftp mode passive command in global configuration mode.

commands.description: To use FXOS SSH, HTTPS, or SNMP on the Firepower 2100 from an ASA data interface, use the fxos permit command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: fxos port

commands.name: gateway

commands.name: gateway-fqdn
commands.description: To configure the FQDN of the ASA.

commands.name: graceful-restart

commands.description: To configure graceful restart for OSPFv3 on a NSF aware ASA, use the graceful-restartUse the no form of the command to disable graceful-restart helper mode.

commands.name: group

commands.name: group-alias
commands.description: To create one or more alternate names by which the user can refer to a tunnel group, use the group-alias command in tunnel-group webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: group-delimiter
commands.description: To enable group name parsing and specify the delimiter to be used when parsing group names from the user names that are received when tunnels are being negotiated, use the group-delimiter command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: group-lock
commands.description: To restrict remote users to access through the tunnel group only, issue the group-lock command in group-policy configuration mode or username configuration mode.

modes: Protocol, network, service, icmp-type, security group, and user object-group configuration modes

commands.name: group-policy
commands.syntax: group-policy name {internal [from group-policy_name] | external server-group server_group password server_password}

commands.name: group-policy attributes
commands.description: To enter the group-policy configuration mode, use the group-policy attributes command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: group-prompt
commands.description: To customize the group prompt of the WebVPN page login box that is displayed to WebVPN users when they connect to the ASA, use the group-prompt command in webvpn customization configuration mode.

commands.name: group-search-timeout

commands.name: group-url
commands.description: To specify incoming URLs or IP addresses for the group, use the group-url command in tunnel-group webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: gsn-limit
commands.description: To specify the maximum number of GPRS support node (GSN) endpoints tracked by the GPRS Tunneling Protocol (GTP) inspection engine, use the gsn-limit command.

commands.name: gtp-u-header-check
commands.description: To check whether the inner payload of a GTP data packet is a valid IP packet and drop it if it is not, use the gtp-u-header-check command in GTP inspection policy map parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: h245-tunnel-block
commands.description: To block H.245 tunneling in H.323, use the h245-tunnel-block command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: hardware-bypass

commands.name: hardware-bypass boot-delay
commands.description: To configure the hardware bypass on the Cisco ISA 3000 to remain active until after the ASA Firepower module boots up, use the hardware-bypass boot-delay command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: hardware-bypass manual

commands.name: health-check

commands.name: health-check application

commands.name: health-check auto-rejoin

commands.name: health-check chassis-heartbeat-delay-rejoin

commands.name: health-check monitor-interface
commands.description: To monitor interfaces, use the health-check monitor-interface command in cluster group configuration mode.

commands.name: hello padding multi-point

commands.name: hello-interval

commands.name: help

commands.name: hidden-parameter

commands.name: hidden-shares

commands.name: hold-time
commands.description: To specify the hold time advertised by the ASA in EIGRP hello packets, use the hold-time command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: homepage

commands.name: homepage use-smart-tunnel

commands.name: host (network object)

commands.name: host (parameters)

commands.name: hostname

commands.name: hostscan image
commands.description: To install or upgrade the Cisco Host Scan distribution package and add it to the running configuration, use the hostscan image command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: hpm topn enable
commands.description: To enable real-time reports in ASDM of the top hosts connecting through the ASA, use the hpm topn enable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: hsi

commands.name: hsi-group
commands.description: To define an HSI group for H.323 protocol inspection and to enter hsi group configuration mode, use the hsi-group command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: hsts enable
commands.description: To configure sending the HTTP Strict Transport Security Header to browsers and other user agents, use the hsts enable command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: hsts max-age
commands.description: When configured to send the HTTP Strict Transport Security Header to browsers or other user agents, (using the hsts enable command), hsts max-age sets the maximum amount of time the ASA will be treated as an HSTS host and accessed securely

commands.name: html-content-filter

commands.name: http (global)

commands.name: http authentication-certificate

commands.name: http connection idle-timeout
commands.description: To set an idle timeout for HTTPS connections to the ASA, including ASDM, clientless VPN, Secure Client, and other clients, use the http connection idle-timeout command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: http redirect

commands.name: http server basic-auth-client

commands.name: http server enable

commands.name: http server idle-timeout

commands.name: http server session-timeout

commands.name: ipv6-prefix
commands.description: To configure the IPv6 prefix for the basic mapping rule in a Mapping Address and Port (MAP) domain, use the ipv6-prefix command in MAP domain basic mapping rule configuration mode.
commands.mode: MAP domain basic mapping rule configuration mode
modes: MAP domain basic mapping rule configuration mode

commands.name: ipv6-split-tunnel-policy
commands.description: To set a IPv6 split tunneling policy, use the ipv6-spli t-tunnel-policy command in group-policy configuration mode.

commands.name: ipv6-vpn-address-assign
commands.description: To specify a method for assigning IPv6 addresses to remote access clients, use the ipv6- vpn-addr-assign command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: ipv6-vpn-filter
commands.description: To specify the name of the IPv6 ACL to use for VPN connections, use the ipv6-vpn-filter command in group-policy configuration or username configuration mode.

commands.name: is-type
commands.description: To configure the routing level for an instance of the IS-IS routing process, use the is-type command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp am-disable
commands.description: To disable inbound aggressive mode connections, use the isakmp am-disable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp disconnect-notify
commands.description: To enable disconnect notification to peers, use the isakmp disconnect-notify command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp enable
commands.description: To enable ISAKMP negotiation on the interface on which the IPsec peer communicates with the ASA, use the isakmp enable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp identity
commands.syntax: isakmp identity {address | hostname | key-id key-id-string | auto}
commands.description: To set the Phase 2 ID to be sent to the peer, use the isakmp identity command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp ipsec-over-tcp
commands.description: To enable IPsec over TCP, use the isakmp ipsec-over-tcp command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp keepalive
commands.description: To configure IKE keepalives, use the isakmp keepalive command in tunnel-group ipsec-attributes configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp nat-traversal
commands.description: To enable NAT traversal globally, check that ISAKMP is enabled (you can enable it with the isakmp enable command) in global configuration mode and then use the isakmp nat-traversal command.

commands.name: isakmp policy authentication
commands.syntax: isakmp policy priority authentication {crack | pre-share | rsa-sig}
commands.description: To specify an authentication method within an IKE policy, use the isakmp policy authentication command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp policy encryption
commands.syntax: isakmp policy priority encryption {aes | aes-192 | aes-256 | des | 3des}
commands.description: To specify the encryption algorithm to use within an IKE policy, use the isakmp policy encryption command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp policy group
commands.description: To specify the Diffie-Hellman group for an IKE policy, use the isakmp policy group command in global configuration mode.To reset the Diffie-Hellman group identifier to the default value, use the no form of this command.

commands.name: isakmp policy hash
commands.description: To specify the hash algorithm for an IKE policy, use the isakmp policy hash command in global configuration mode.To reset the hash algorithm to the default value of SHA-1, use the no form of this command.

commands.name: isakmp policy lifetime
commands.description: To specify the lifetime of an IKE security association before it expires, use the isakmp policy lifetime command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: isakmp reload-wait
commands.description: To enable waiting for all active sessions to voluntarily terminate before rebooting the ASA, use the isakmp reload-wait command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: isis priority
commands.description: To configure the priority of designated ASAs on an interface, use the isis priority command in interface isis configuration mode.

commands.name: isis protocol shutdown
commands.description: To disable the IS-IS protocol so that it cannot form adjacencies on a specified interface and place the IP address of the interface into the LSP that is generated by the ASA, use the isis protocol shutdown command in interface isis configuration mode.

commands.name: isis retransmit-interval
commands.description: To configure the amount of time between retransmission of each IS-IS LSP, use the isis retransmit-interval command in interface isis configuration mode.

commands.name: isis retransmit-throttle-interval
commands.description: To configure the amount of time between retransmissions of each IS-IS LSP on an interface, use the isis retransmit-throttle-interval command in interface isis configuration mode.

commands.name: isis tag
commands.description: To set a tag on the IP address configured for an interface when this IP prefix is put into an IS-IS LSP, use the isis tag command in interface isis configuration mode.

commands.name: issuer
commands.description: Note

commands.name: issuer-name
commands.description: To specify the issuer name DN of all issued certificates, use the issuer-name command in local certificate authority (CA) server configuration mode.

commands.name: java-trustpoint
commands.description: To configure the WebVPN Java object signing facility to use a PKCS12 certificate and keying material from a specified trustpoint location, use the java-trustpoint command in webvpn configuration mode.To remove a trustpoint for Java object signing, use the no form of this command.

commands.name: join-failover-group
commands.description: To assign a context to a failover group, use the join-failover-group command in context configuration mode.

commands.name: jumbo-frame reservation
commands.description: To enable jumbo frames for supported models, use the jumbo-frame reservation command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: kcd-server
commands.syntax: kcd-server aaa-server-group_name username user_id password password [validate-server-certificate]
commands.description: To configure Kerberos Constrained Delegation (KCD) for clientless SSL remote access VPN, use the kcd-server command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: keepout
commands.description: To present an administrator-defined message rather than a login page for new user sessions (when the ASA undergoes a maintenance or troubleshooting period), use the keepout command in webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: kerberos-realm
commands.description: To specify the realm name for this Kerberos server, use the kerberos-realm command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: kernel crash-dump
commands.description: To enable the secondary crash dump kernel, enter the kernel crash-dump command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: key (aaa-server host)
commands.description: To specify the server secret value used to authenticate the NAS to the AAA server, use the key command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: key (cluster group)
commands.description: To set an authentication key for control traffic on the cluster control link, use the key command in cluster group configuration mode.

commands.name: key chain
commands.syntax: key chain key-chain-name key key-id key-string {0 | 8} key-string-text cryptographic-algorithm md5 [accept-lifetime [local | start-time] [duration {duration value | infinite | end-time}]
commands.description: To configure rotating keys for authenticating IGP peers, use the key chain command in the global configuration mode.

commands.name: key config-key password-encryption
commands.description: To set the master passphrase used for generating the encryption key to securely store plain text passwords in encrypted format, use the key config-key password-encryption command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: key-hash
commands.description: To manually add a hashed SSH host key for a server for the on-board Secure Copy (SCP) client, use the key-hash command in server configuration mode.

commands.name: key-string
commands.description: To manually add a public SSH host key for a server for the on-board Secure Copy (SCP) client, use the key-string command in server configuration mode.

commands.name: keypair
commands.syntax: [no] keypair name | [rsa modulus | 2048 | 4096] | [ecdsa elliptic-curve 256 | 384 | 521] | [eddsa edwards-curve Ed25519]
commands.description: To specify the key pair whose public key is to be certified, use the keypair command in crypto ca trustpoint configuration mode.

commands.name: keysize
commands.description: To specify the size of the public and private keys generated by the local Certificate Authority (CA) server at user certificate enrollment, use the keysize command in ca-server configuration mode.

commands.name: keysize server
commands.description: To specify the size of the public and private keys generated by the local Certificate Authority (CA) server for configuring the size of the CA keypair, use the keysize server command in ca-server configuration mode.

commands.name: kill
commands.description: To terminate a Telnet session, use the kill command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: l2tp tunnel hello
commands.description: To specify the interval between hello messages on L2TP over IPsec connections, use the l2tp tunnel hello command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: lacp max-bundle
commands.description: To specify the maximum number of active interfaces allowed in the EtherChannel channel group, use the lacp max-bundle command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: lacp port-priority
commands.description: To set the priority for a physical interface in an EtherChannel, use the lacp port-priority command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: lacp rate
commands.description: To sets the rate at which the interface receives LACP data units for a physical interface in an EtherChannel, use the lacp rate command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: lacp system-priority
commands.description: For EtherChannels, to set the LACP system priority globally for the ASA, use the lacp system-priority command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-attribute-map
commands.description: To bind an existing mapping configuration to an LDAP host, use the ldap-attribute-map command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-base-dn
commands.description: To specify the location in the LDAP hierarchy where the server should begin searching when it receives an authorization request, use the ldap-base-dn command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-defaults
commands.description: To define LDAP default values, use the ldap-defaults command in crl configure configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-dn
commands.description: To pass a X.500 distinguished name and password to an LDAP server that requires authentication for CRL retrieval, use the ldap-dn command in crl configure configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-group-base-dn
commands.description: To specify the base group in the Active Directory hierarchy used by dynamic access policies for group searches, use the ldap-group-base-dn command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-login-dn
commands.description: To specify the name of the directory object that the system should bind this as, use the ldap-login-dn command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-login-password
commands.description: To specify the login password for the LDAP server, use the ldap-login-password command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-naming-attribute
commands.description: To specify the Relative Distinguished Name attribute, use the ldap-naming-attribute command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-over-ssl
commands.description: To establish a secure SSL connection between the ASA and the LDAP server, use the ldap-over-ssl command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: ldap-scope
commands.description: To specify the extent of the search in the LDAP hierarchy that the server should make when it receives an authorization request, use the ldap-scope command in aaa-server host configuration mode.

commands.name: leap-bypass
commands.description: To enable LEAP Bypass, use the leap-bypass enable command in group-policy configuration mode.

commands.name: license
commands.description: To configure the authentication key that the ASA sends to the Cloud Web Security proxy servers to indicate from which organization the request comes, use the license command in scansafe general-options configuration mode.

commands.name: license smart
commands.description: To set the smart licensing entitlement request, use the license smart command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license smart deregister
commands.description: To deregister the device from the Cisco License Authority for smart licensing, use the license smart deregister command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: license smart plr set
commands.syntax: license smart plr set {ASAV_5_UNIVERSAL | ASAV_10_UNIVERSAL | ASAV_30_UNIVERSAL | ASAV_50_UNIVERSAL | ASAV_100_UNIVERSAL | ASAV_U_UNIVERSAL}
commands.description: To configure permanent license reservation irrespective of the RAM and vCPU (flexible permanent license reservation mode), use the license smart plr set command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license smart register
commands.description: To register the device with the Cisco License Authority for smart licensing, use the license smart register command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: license smart renew
commands.description: To renew the registration or license entitlement authorization for smart licensing, use the license smart renew command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: license smart reservation
commands.description: To enable permanent license reservation, use the license smart reservation command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license smart reservation cancel
commands.description: To cancel a permanent license reservation request if you have not yet entered the code in the Smart Software Manager, use the license smart reservation cancel command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: license smart reservation install
commands.description: To enter a permanent license reservation authorization code received from the Smart Software Manager, use the license smart reservation install command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: license smart reservation return
commands.description: To generate a return code to return the license to the Smart Software Manager, use the license smart reservation return command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: license smart reservation universal
commands.description: To request the license code to enter in the Smart Software Manager, use the license smart reservation universal command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: license-server address
commands.syntax: license-server address address secret secret [port port]
commands.description: To identify the shared licensing server IP address and shared secret for use by a participant, use the license-server address command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license-server backup address
commands.description: To identify the shared licensing backup server IP address for use by a participant, use the license-server backup address command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license-server backup backup-id
commands.syntax: license-server backup address backup-id serial_number [ha-backup-id ha_serial_number]
commands.description: To identify the shared licensing backup server in the main shared licensing server configuration, use the license-server backup backup-id command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license-server backup enable
commands.description: To enable this unit to be the shared licensing backup server, use the license-server backup enable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license-server enable
commands.description: To identify this unit as a shared licensing server, use the license-server enable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license-server port
commands.description: To set the port on which the shared licensing server listens for SSL connections from participants, use the license-server port command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license-server refresh-interval
commands.description: To set the refresh interval provided to participants to set how often they should communicate with the shared licensing server, use the license-server refresh-interval command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: license-server secret
commands.description: To set the shared secret on the shared licensing server, use the license-server secret command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: lifetime (ca server mode)
commands.description: To specify the length of time that the Local Certificate Authority (CA) certificate, each issued user certificates, or the Certificate Revocation List (CRL) is valid, use the lifetime command in ca server configuration mode.

commands.name: lifetime (ikev2 policy mode)
commands.description: To specify the encryption algorithm in an IKEv2 security association (SA) for AnyConnect IPsec connections, use the encryption command in IKEv2 policy configuration mode.

commands.name: limit-resource
commands.description: To specify a resource limit for a class in multiple context mode, use the limit-resource command in class configuration mode.

commands.name: lmfactor
commands.description: To set a revalidation policy for caching objects that have only the last-modified timestamp, and no other server-set expiration values, use the lmfactor command in cache configuration mode.

commands.name: load-monitor
commands.description: To configure cluster traffic load monitoring, use the load-monitor command in cluster configuration mode.

commands.name: local-base-url
commands.description: (Optional) Configures the local base URL of the SAML service provider for VPN authentication.

commands.name: local-domain-bypass
commands.description: To configure local domains for which DNS requests should bypass Cisco Umbrella, use the local-domain-bypass command in Umbrella configuration mode.

commands.name: local-unit
commands.description: To provide a name for this cluster member, use the local-unit command in cluster group configuration mode.

commands.name: location-logging
commands.description: To have GTP inspection log the location and change of location for mobile stations, use the location-logging command in GTP inspection policy map parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: log
commands.description: When using the Modular Policy Framework, log packets that match a match command or class map by using the log command in match or class configuration mode.

commands.name: log-adj-changes
commands.description: To configure the router to send a syslog message when an OSPF neighbor goes up or down, use the log-adj-changes command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: log-adjacency-changes
commands.description: To configure the router to send a syslog message when an OSPFv3 neighbor goes up or down, use the log-adjacency-changes command in IPv6 router configuration mode.

commands.name: logging asdm
commands.description: To send syslog messages to the ASDM log buffer, use the logging asdm command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging asdm-buffer-size
commands.description: To specify the number of syslog messages retained in the ASDM log buffer, use the logging asdm-buffer-size command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging buffer-size
commands.description: To specify the size of the log buffer, use the logging buffer-size command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging buffered
commands.description: To enable the ASA to send syslog messages to the log buffer, use the logging buffered command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging class
commands.syntax: logging class class destination level [destination level . . .]
commands.description: To configure the maximum severity level per logging destination for a message class, use the logging class command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging console
commands.description: To enable the ASA to display syslog messages in console sessions, use the logging console command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging debug-trace
commands.description: To redirect debugging messages to logs as syslog message 711001 issued at severity level 7, use the logging debug-trace command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging debug-trace persistent
commands.description: To enable debug syslogs active in a particular session to be logged, even after the session ends, use the logging debug-trace persistent command in the global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging device-id
commands.syntax: logging device-id {cluster-id | context-name | hostname ipaddress interface_name [system] | string text}
commands.description: To configure the ASA to include a device ID in non-EMBLEM-format syslog messages, use the logging device-id command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging emblem
commands.description: To use the EMBLEM format for syslog messages sent to destinations other than a syslog server, use the logging emblem command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging enable
commands.description: To enable logging for all configured output locations, use the logging enable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging facility
commands.description: To specify the logging facility used for messages sent to syslog servers, use the logging facility command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging flash-bufferwrap
commands.description: To enable the ASA to write the log buffer to flash memory every time the buffer is full of messages that have never been saved, use the logging flash-bufferwrap command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging flash-maximum-allocation
commands.description: To specify the maximum amount of flash memory that the ASA uses to store log data, use the logging flash-maximum-allocation command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging flash-minimum-free
commands.description: To specify the minimum amount of free flash memory that must exist before the ASA saves a new log file, use the logging flash-minimum-free command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging flow-export-syslogs
commands.description: To enable or disable all of the syslog messages that NetFlow captures, use the logging flow-export-syslogs command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging from-address
commands.description: To specify the sender e-mail address for syslog messages sent by the ASA, use the logging from-address command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging ftp-bufferwrap
commands.description: To enable the ASA to send the log buffer to an FTP server every time the buffer is full of messages that have never been saved, use the logging ftp-bufferwrap command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging ftp-server
commands.syntax: logging ftp-server ftp_server path username [0 | 8] password
commands.description: To specify details about the FTP server that the ASA sends log buffer data to when logging ftp-bufferwrap is enabled, use the logging ftp-server command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging hide username
commands.description: To hide usernames (for example, “*****”) in syslogs when the username’s validity is unknown, use the logging hide username command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging history
commands.syntax: logging history [rate-limit number interval level level | logging_list | level]
commands.description: To enable SNMP logging and specify which messages are to be sent to SNMP servers, use the logging history command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging host
commands.syntax: logging host interface_name syslog_ip [tcp [/ port] | udp [/ port]] [format emblem | timestamp [legacy | rfc5424]] [secure [reference-identity reference_identity_name]]
commands.description: To define a syslog server, use the logging host command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging list
commands.syntax: logging list name {level level [class event_class] | message start_id [-end_id]}
commands.description: To create a logging list to use in other commands to specify messages by various criteria (logging level, event class, and message IDs), use the logging list command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging mail
commands.description: To enable the ASA to send syslog messages by e-mail and to determine which messages are sent by e-mail, use the logging mail command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging message
commands.description: To enable logging of a syslog message, or to change the level of a message, use the logging message command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging message standby
commands.description: To unblock a specific syslog message that was previously blocked from being generated on a standby unit, use the logging message standby command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging monitor
commands.description: To enable the ASA to display syslog messages in SSH and Telnet sessions, use the logging monitor command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging permit-hostdown
commands.description: To make the status of a TCP-based syslog server irrelevant to new user sessions, use the logging permit-hostdown command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging queue
commands.description: To specify how many syslog messages the ASA may hold in its queue before processing them according to the logging configuration, use the logging queue command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging rate-limit
commands.syntax: logging rate-limit {unlimited | dynamic {block value [message limit value]} | {num [interval]} | message {syslog_id | level severity_level}}
commands.description: To limit the rate at which syslog messages are generated, use the logging rate-limit command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: logging recipient-address
commands.description: To specify the receiving e-mail address for syslog messages sent by the ASA, use the logging recipient-address command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging savelog
commands.description: To save the log buffer to flash memory, use the logging savelog command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: logging standby
commands.description: To enable the failover standby ASA to send syslog messages to logging destinations, use the logging standby command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging tcp-block-reduction
commands.description: To manage block depletion that occurs due to syslog messages or to deduce the queue size of the logging queue, use logging tcp-block-reduction in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging timestamp
commands.description: To specify that syslog messages should include the date and time that the messages was generated, use the logging timestamp command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: logging trap
commands.description: To specify which syslog messages the ASA sends to a syslog server, use the logging trap command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: login
commands.description: To log into privileged EXEC mode using the local user database (see the username command) or to change user names, use the login command in user EXEC mode.

commands.name: login-button
commands.description: To customize the Login button of the WebVPN page login box that is displayed to WebVPN users when they connect to the security appliance, use the login-button command from webvpn customization configuration mode.

commands.name: login-message
commands.description: To customize the login message of the WebVPN page displayed to WebVPN users when they connect to the security appliance, use the login-message command from webvpn customization configuration mode.

commands.name: login-title
commands.description: To customize the title of the login box on the WebVPN page displayed to WebVPN users, use the login-title command from webvpn customization configuration mode.

commands.name: logo
commands.description: To customize the logo on the WebVPN page displayed to WebVPN users when they connect to the security appliance, use the logo command from webvpn customization mode.

commands.name: logout
commands.description: To exit from the CLI, use the logout command in user EXEC mode.

commands.name: logout-message
commands.description: To customize the logout message of the WebVPN logout screen that is displayed to WebVPN users when they logout from WebVPN service, use the logout-message command from webvpn customization configuration mode.

commands.name: lsp-full suppress
commands.description: To control which routes are suppressed when the link-state protocol data unit (PDU) becomes full, use the lsp-full suppress command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: lsp-gen-interval
commands.description: To customize IS-IS throttling of LSP generation, use the lsp-gen-interval command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: lsp-refresh-interval
commands.description: To set the LSP refresh interval, use the lsp-refresh-interval command in router isis configuration mode.

commands.name: mac address
commands.description: To specify the virtual MAC addresses for the active and standby units, use the mac address command in failover group configuration mode.

commands.name: mac-address
commands.syntax: mac-address {mac_address [standby mac_address | site-id number [site-ip ip_address]] | cluster-pool pool_name}
commands.description: To manually assign a private MAC address to an interface or subinterface, use the mac-address command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: mac-address auto
commands.description: To automatically assign private MAC addresses to each shared context interface, use the mac-address auto command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: mac-address pool
commands.description: To add a MAC address pool for use on an individual interface in an ASA cluster, use the mac-address pool command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: mac-address-table aging-time
commands.description: To set the timeout for MAC address table entries, use the mac-address-table aging-time command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: mac-address-table static
commands.description: To add a static entry to the MAC address table, use the mac-address-table static command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: mac-learn disable
commands.description: To disable MAC address learning for an interface, use the mac-learn command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: mac-learn flood
commands.description: To enable flooding for unknown MAC addresses for non IPv4/IPv6 packets, use the mac-learn flood command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: mac-list
commands.description: To specify a list of MAC addresses to be used to exempt MAC addresses from authentication and/or authorization, use the mac- list command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: mail-relay
commands.description: To configure a local domain name, use the mail-relay command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: management-access
commands.description: To allow management access to an interface other than the one from which you entered the ASA when using VPN, use the management-access command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: management-only
commands.description: To set an interface to accept management traffic only, use the management-only command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: map-domain
commands.description: To configure a Mapping Address and Port (MAP) domain, use the map-domain command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: map-name
commands.description: To map a user-defined attribute name to a Cisco attribute name, use the map-name command in ldap-attribute-map configuration mode.

commands.name: map-value
commands.description: To map a user-defined value to a Cisco LDAP value, use the map-value command in ldap-attribute-map configuration mode.

commands.name: mapping-service
commands.syntax: mapping-service listening-interface interface [listening-port port] uc-ime-interface interface
commands.description: To configure a mapping service for the Cisco Intercompany Media Engine proxy, use the mapping-service command in UC-IME configuration mode.

commands.name: mask
commands.description: When using the Modular Policy Framework, mask out part of the packet that matches a match command or class map by using the mask command in match or class configuration mode.

commands.name: mask-banner
commands.description: To obfuscate the server banner, use the mask-banner command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: mask-syst-reply
commands.description: To hide the FTP server response from clients, use the mask-syst-reply command in FTP map configuration mode, which is accessible by using the ftp-map command.

commands.name: match access-list
commands.description: When using the Modular Policy Framework, use an access list to identify traffic to which you want to apply actions by using the match access-list command in class-map configuration mode.

commands.name: match any
commands.description: When using the Modular Policy Framework, match all traffic to which you want to apply actions by using the match any command in class-map configuration mode.

commands.name: match apn
commands.description: To configure a match condition for an access point name in GTP messages, use the match apn command in policy-map configuration mode.

commands.name: match application-id
commands.description: To configure a match condition for the Diameter application identifier of Diameter messages, use the match application-id command in class-map or policy-map configuration mode.

commands.name: match as-path
commands.description: To match a BGP autonomous system path access list, use the match as-path command in route-map configuration mode.

commands.name: match avp

commands.name: pwd

commands.name: queue-limit (priority-queue)

commands.name: queue-limit (tcp-map)

commands.name: quick-start

commands.name: quit

commands.name: radius-reject-message

commands.name: radius-with-expiry
commands.description: Note

commands.name: raid

commands.name: range

commands.name: ras-rcf-pinholes

commands.name: rate-limit

commands.name: re-xauth

commands.name: record-route

commands.name: regex

commands.name: reload

commands.name: request-data-size

commands.name: reserve-port-protect

commands.name: reserved-bits

commands.name: reset

commands.name: resolver

commands.name: responder-only

commands.name: rest-api

commands.name: restore

commands.name: retry-interval
commands.description: To configure the amount of time between retry attempts for a particular AAA server designated in a previous aaa-server host command, use the retry-interval command in aaa-server host mode.

commands.name: reval-period
commands.description: To specify the interval between each successful posture validation in a NAC Framework session, use the reval-period command in nac-policy-nac-framework configuration mode.

commands.name: revert webvpn all

commands.name: revert webvpn AnyConnect-customization
commands.syntax: revert webvpn AnyConnect-customization type type platform platform name name
commands.description: To remove a file from the ASA that customizes the Secure client GUI , use the revert webvpn AnyConnect-customization command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: revert webvpn customization
commands.description: To remove a customization object from the ASA cache memory, enter the revert webvpn customization command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: revert webvpn plug-in protocol
commands.description: To remove a plug-in from the flash device of the ASA, enter the revert webvpn plug-in protocol command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: revert webvpn translation-table
commands.syntax: revert webvpn translation-table translationdomain language language
commands.description: To remove a translation table from the ASA flash memory, enter the revert webvpn translation-table command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: revert webvpn webcontent

commands.name: router eigrp

commands.name: router isis
commands.description: To enable the IS-IS routing protocol and to specify an IS-IS process, use the router isis command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: router ospf

commands.name: router-alert

commands.name: service-module

commands.name: vdi
commands.syntax: vdi type citrix url url domain domain username username password password
commands.description: To provide secure remote access for Citrix Receiver applications running on mobile devices to XenApp and XenDesktop VDI servers through the ASA, use the vdi command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: To verify the checksum of a file, use the verify command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: verify-header
commands.description: To allow only known IPv6 extension headers and enforces the order of IPv6 extension headers, use the verify-header command in parameters configuration mode.

commands.name: version
commands.description: To specify the version of RIP used globally by the ASA, use the version command in router configuration mode.

commands.name: virtual http
commands.description: To configure a virtual HTTP server, use the virtual http command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: virtual telnet
commands.description: To configure a virtual Telnet server on the ASA, use the virtual telnet command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vlan (group-policy)
commands.description: To assign a VLAN to a group policy, use the vlan command in group-policy configuration mode.

commands.name: vlan (interface)
commands.description: To assign a VLAN ID to a subinterface, use the vlan command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: vpdn group
commands.syntax: vpdn group group_name {localname username | request dialout pppoe | ppp authentication {chap | mschap | pap}}
commands.description: To create or edit a vpdn group and configure PPPoE client settings, use the vpdn group command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpdn username
commands.description: To create a username and password pair for PPPoE connections, use the vpdn username command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn load-balancing
commands.description: To enter vpn load-balancing mode, in which you can configure VPN load balancing and related functions, use the vpn load-balancing command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-access-hours
commands.description: To associate a group policy with a configured time-range policy, use the vpn-access-hours command in group-policy configuration mode or username configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-addr-assign
commands.description: To specify a method for assigning IPv4 addresses to remote access clients, use the vpn-addr-assign command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-filter
commands.description: To specify the name of the ACL to use for VPN connections, use the vpn -filter command in group policy or username mode.

commands.name: vpn-framed-ip-address
commands.description: To specify the IPv4 address to assign to an individual user, use the vpn -framed-ip-address command in username mode.

commands.name: vpn-framed-ipv6-address
commands.description: Use the vpn -framed-ipv6-address command in username mode to assign a dedicated IPv6 address to a user.

commands.name: vpn-group-policy
commands.description: To have a user inherit attributes from a configured group policy, use the vpn-group-policy command in username configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-idle-timeout
commands.description: To configure a user timeout period use the vpn-idle-timeout command in group-policy configuration mode or in username configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-mode
commands.description: To configure distributed site-to-site VPN mode for a cluster, use the vpn-mode command in cluster group configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-session-timeout
commands.description: To configure a maximum amount of time allowed for VPN connections, use the vpn-session-timeout command in group-policy configuration mode or in username configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-sessiondb
commands.description: To specify the maximum number of VPN sessions or Secure Client VPN sessions, use the vpn-sessiondb command from global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-sessiondb logoff
commands.syntax: vpn-sessiondb logoff {all | anyconnect | email-proxy | index index_number | ipaddress IPaddr | l2l | name username | protocol protocol-name | ra-ikev1-ipsec | ra-ikev2-ipsec | tunnel-group groupname | vpn-lb | webvpn}[noconfirm]
commands.description: To log off all or selected VPN sessions, use the vpn-sessiondb logoff command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-simultaneous-logins
commands.description: To configure the number of simultaneous logins permitted for a user, use the vpn-simultaneous-logins command in group-policy configuration mode or username configuration mode.

commands.name: vpn-tunnel-protocol
commands.description: To configure a VPN tunnel type (IPsec with IKEv1 or IKEv2, L2TP over IPsec, SSL, or clientless SSL), use the vpn-tunnel-protocol command in group-policy configuration mode or username configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient connect
commands.description: To attempt to establish an Easy VPN Remote connection to the configured server or servers, use the vpnclient connect command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient enable
commands.description: To enable the Easy VPN Remote feature, use the vpnclient enable command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient ipsec-over-tcp
commands.description: To configure the ASA running as an Easy VPN Remote hardware client to use TCP-encapsulated IPsec, use the vpnclient ipsec-over-tcp command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient mac-exempt
commands.syntax: vpnclient mac-exempt mac_addr_1 mac_mask_1 [mac_addr_2 mac_mask_2...mac_addr_n mac_mask_n]
commands.description: To exempt devices behind an Easy VPN Remote connection from individual user authentication requirements, use the vpnclient mac-exempt command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient management
commands.syntax: vpnclient management tunnel ip_addr_1 ip_mask_1 [ip_addr_2 ip_mask_2...ip_addr_n ip_mask_n]
commands.description: To generate IPsec tunnels for management access to the Easy VPN Remote hardware client, use the vpnclient management command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient mode
commands.description: To configure the Easy VPN Remote connection for either client mode or network extension mode, use the vpnclient mode command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient nem-st-autoconnect
commands.description: To configure the Easy VPN Remote connection to automatically initiate IPsec data tunnels when NEM and split tunneling are configured, use the vpnclient nem-st-autoconnect command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient server
commands.description: To configure the primary and secondary IPsec servers, for the Easy VPN Remote connection, use the vpnclient server command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient server-certificate
commands.description: To configure the Easy VPN Remote connection to accept only connections to Easy VPN servers with the specific certificates specified by the certificate map, use the vpnclient server-certificate command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient trustpoint
commands.description: To configure the RSA identity certificate to be used by the Easy VPN Remote connection, use the vpnclient trustpoint command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient username
commands.syntax: vpnclient username xauth_username password xauth password
commands.description: To configure the VPN username and password for the Easy VPN Remote connection, use the vpnclient username command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnclient vpngroup
commands.description: To configure the VPN tunnel group name and password for the Easy VPN Remote connection, use the vpnclient vpngroup command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: vpnsetup
commands.description: To display a list of steps for configuring VPN connections on the ASA, use the vpnsetup command from global configuration mode.

commands.name: vtep-nve
commands.description: To associate a VXLAN VNI interface with the VTEP source interface, use the vtep-nve command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: vxlan port
commands.description: To set the VXLAN UDP port, use the vxlan port command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: wccp
commands.description: To allocate space and to enable support of the specified Web Cache Communication Protocol (WCCP) service for participation in a service group, use the wccp command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: wccp redirect
commands.syntax: wccp interface interface_name service redirect in
commands.description: To enable packet redirection on the ingress of an interface using Web Cache Communication Protocol (WCCP), use the wccp redirect command.

commands.name: web update-type
commands.description: To specify the address types (IPv4 or IPv6) that you want to update when using the DDNS Web update method, use the web update-type command in ddns update method configuration mode.

commands.name: web update-url
commands.description: To specify the web update method for DDNS along with the web type URL, use the web update-url command in ddns update method configuration mode.

commands.name: web-agent-url
commands.description: Note

commands.name: web-applications
commands.description: To customize the Web Application box of the WebVPN Home page that is displayed to authenticated WebVPN users, use the web-applications command from webvpn customization mode:

commands.name: web-bookmarks
commands.syntax: web-bookmarks {link {style value} | title {style value | text value}}
commands.description: To customize the Web Bookmarks title or links on the WebVPN Home page that is displayed to authenticated WebVPN users, use the web-bookmarks command from webvpn customization mode:

commands.name: webvpn (global)
commands.description: To enter webvpn mode, in global configuration mode, enter the webvpn command.

commands.name: webvpn (group-policy attributes, username attributes)
commands.description: To enter this webvpn mode, use the webvpn command in group-policy attributes configuration mode or in username attributes configuration mode.
commands.mode: Group-policy attributes configuration, Username attributes configuration

commands.name: whitelist
commands.description: For Cloud Web Security, to perform the whitelist action on the class of traffic, use the whitelist command in class configuration mode.

commands.name: who
commands.description: To display active Telnet administration sessions on the ASA, use the who command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: window-variation
commands.description: To drop a connection with a window size variation, use the window-variation command in tcp-map configuration mode.

commands.name: wins-server
commands.description: To set the IP address of the primary and secondary WINS servers, use the wins-server command in group-policy configuration mode.

commands.name: without-csd
commands.description: To exempt certain users from running the Hostscan application of Cisco Secure Desktop on a per connection profile basis if they enter one of the entries in the group-urls table to establish the VPN session, use the without-csd command in tunnel webvpn configuration mode.

commands.name: write erase
commands.description: To erase the startup configuration, use the write erase command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: write memory
commands.description: To save the running configuration to the startup configuration, use the write memory command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: write net
commands.description: To save the running configuration to a TFTP server, use the write net command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: write standby
commands.description: To copy the ASA or context running configuration to the failover standby unit, use the write standby command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: write terminal
commands.description: To show the running configuration on the terminal, use the write terminal command in privileged EXEC mode.

commands.name: xlate block-allocation
commands.syntax: xlate block-allocation {size value | maximum-per-host number | pba-interim-logging seconds}
commands.description: To configure the port block allocation characteristics for carrier-grade or large-scale PAT, use the xlate block-allocation command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: xlate per-session
commands.syntax: xlate per-session {permit | deny}{tcp | udp} source_ip [operator src_port] destination_ip operator dest_port
commands.description: To use multi-session PAT, use the xlate per-session command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: zone
commands.description: To add a traffic zone, use the zone command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: zone-member
commands.description: To add an interface to a traffic zone, use the zone-member command in interface configuration mode.

commands.name: zonelabs-integrity fail-close
commands.description: To configure the ASA so that connections to VPN clients close when the connection between the ASA and the Zone Labs Integrity Firewall Server fails, use the zonelabs-integrity fail-close command in global configuration mode.To reinstate the default whereby the VPN connections remain open on failure of the Zone Labs co…

commands.name: zonelabs-integrity fail-open
commands.description: To keep remote VPN client connections to the ASA open after the connection between the ASA and the Zone Labs Integrity Firewall Server fails, use the zonelabs-integrity fail-open command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: zonelabs-integrity fail-timeout
commands.description: To specify the time in seconds before the ASA declares a nonresponsive Zone Labs Integrity Firewall Server unreachable, use the zonelabs-integrity fail-timeout command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: zonelabs-integrity interface
commands.description: To specify an ASA interface for communication with the Zone Labs Integrity Server, use the zonelabs-integrity interface command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: zonelabs-integrity port
commands.description: To specify a port on the ASA for communicating with a Zone Labs Integrity Firewall Server, use the zonelabs-integrity port command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: zonelabs-integrity server-address
commands.description: To add Zone Labs Integrity Firewall Servers to the ASA configuration, use the zonelabs-integrity server-address command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: zonelabs-integrity ssl-certificate-port
commands.description: To specify an ASA port to which the Zone Labs Integrity Firewall Server will connect when retrieving an SSL certificate, use the zonelabs-integrity ssl-certificate-port command in global configuration mode.

commands.name: zonelabs-integrity ssl-client-authentication
commands.description: To enable authentication of the Zone Labs Integrity Firewall Server SSL certificate by the ASA, use the zonelabs-integrity ssl-client-authentication command in global configuration mode with the enable argument.
